title: The Internet Leaves Your Phone
script: It is 2031. Your phone is still at home. Your glasses place directions on the pavement. The bus time floats above the stop. At lunch, the menu translates before you finish reading. Technology has become almost invisible. Then someone says hello. A name appears, followed by where you met and what you discussed. A permission asks whether you want to remember every conversation. You notice there is no permission for everyone else. You can finally put your phone down. Would you turn People Memory on?

viewerGoal: Consider the human consequence and choose a boundary.
hooks: It is 2031. Your phone is still at home.
Your glasses remember this stranger. Did they agree?
You left your phone home. The internet came anyway.
strongestHook: It is 2031. Your phone is still at home.
directorBrief: Direct this as a human story about Glasses show a menu, transit and directions; a People Memory permission changes the story. Emotional movement: wonder → consent. Open with a recognisable person or object, introduce one consequence, then leave the final choice unresolved. Fictional dates and interfaces are scenario details. Facts must be separately sourced; use a small persistent POSSIBLE FUTURE label, never a news-like breaking banner.
effort: 60–120 minutes asset production and edit; no audio included.
protocol: Produce original story assets, review factual grounding, verify every future claim is conditional or explicitly fictional, then inspect continuity and safe zones. No real-world experiment outcome is claimed.
evidenceRequirements: Verify present smart-glasses displays; persistent people-memory story is speculative.
